components.css: .ds-langs { position: relative; display: inline-block; } .ds-langs select { appearance: none; border: 2px solid var(--ink, #1e1e1e); border-radius: 8px; background: transparent; color: var(--ink, #1e1e1e); font-family: 'Barlow Condensed', 'Roboto Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; letter-spacing: 0.02em; padding: 8px 30px 8px 12px; } .ds-langs select option { color: #1e1e1e; background: #fff; } .ds-langs::after { content: ''; position: absolute; right: 12px; top: 50%; width: 7px; height: 7px; border-right: 2px solid var(--ink, #1e1e1e); border-bottom: 2px solid var(--ink, #1e1e1e); transform: translateY(-70%) rotate(45deg); pointer-events: none; } .ds-langs select:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus, #005387); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Step Marker
components.description: Numbered step: yellow square, black outline, condensed numeral.
components.css: .ds-steps { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; counter-reset: s; display: flex; gap: 24px; } .ds-steps li { counter-increment: s; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; font-family: 'Barlow Condensed', 'Roboto Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif; font-size: 26px; } .ds-steps li::before { content: counter(s); display: grid; place-items: center; width: 44px; height: 44px; border: 2px solid #1e1e1e; border-radius: 6px; background: #f7ba0b; color: #1e1e1e; font-weight: 700; }

narrative.overview:
Parkzettel looks and behaves like traffic signage. Its job is to be understood at a glance by a stranger standing next to a car, often outdoors, in a hurry, possibly in a language that isn't the owner's. So every element says one thing, in regulated colors, at a size and contrast that survive glare. Nothing is there for decoration that a road sign wouldn't carry.

The mood is direct, legible, utilitarian and official without being stern: it has the authority of a sign, not the tone of a parking fine. Type is condensed and heavy where it reads as signage (plate, headings, buttons) and calm and open where people read (body text). Controls are flat plates with thick outlines and generous targets. Surfaces are separated by hard rules, not containers. Depth exists only where the screen depicts a real object: the printed sticker, the plate, the phone.

Light mode sits on Traffic White; dark mode on Asphalt. Both keep the same yellow, plate blue and messenger colors, because those are recognized by their color in the real world.
keyCharacteristics: One signal color, Traffic Yellow, marks the thing to do; everything else is black, white and grey.
Two faces: Barlow Condensed for anything that reads as a sign, Barlow for reading.
Flat, hard-edged controls with 2px outlines and 8px corners; big tap targets.
Sections divided by 3px black rules, never by cards or shadows.
Real objects (sticker, plate, phone) are the only things with shadows.
Built for a phone held next to a car: 360px and up, dark mode, outdoor contrast.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Traffic Yellow marks the action or the thing to notice. It is never a background wash for whole sections, and a screen never has two competing yellow calls to action of equal weight.

rules.name: The Plate Blue Rule
rules.body: EU Plate Blue appears only on the license plate. It is not a brand or link color.

rules.name: The True Colors Rule
rules.body: Messenger and plate colors are not restyled, tinted or used elsewhere; their meaning comes from matching the real world.

rules.name: The Sign Voice Rule
rules.body: If it should be read from a step away (plate, headings, buttons, sticker text), it is Barlow Condensed. If it should be read up close, it is Barlow. No third family.

rules.name: The No Shouting Rule
rules.body: Emphasis comes from the condensed face and weight, not from all-caps labels or tracked-out eyebrow text. Only the plate is uppercase.

rules.name: The Even Lines Rule
rules.body: Headings use `text-wrap: balance`; paragraphs and list items use `text-wrap: pretty`, so no line ends on a single orphaned word.

rules.name: The Real Objects Rule
rules.body: Only things that exist in the physical world (sticker, plate, phone) cast shadows. Buttons, inputs, notes, menus and sections stay flat.

dos: **Do** keep one Traffic Yellow call to action per view and give it black text.
**Do** separate sections with a 3px Traffic Black rule instead of containers.
**Do** use Barlow Condensed for plates, headings, buttons and sticker text, Barlow for reading text.
**Do** keep every tap target at least 44px tall (46px for buttons), and scanner-page actions at 66px.
**Do** check every page at 320px wide: nothing may scroll sideways.
**Do** show a 3px Signal Blue focus ring with a 2px offset on every interactive element.
**Do** keep messenger and EU plate colors true to the real world.
**Do** respect reduced motion: the only motion is a short press feedback.
donts: **Don't** wrap content in generic cards with soft shadows; the system is flat.
**Don't** give interface surfaces shadows; only the sticker, plate and phone cast them.
**Don't** use all-caps tracked eyebrow labels above headings.
**Don't** use EU Plate Blue, WhatsApp Green or Telegram Blue as general accents.
**Don't** add decorative motion, gradients or illustrations; a road sign has none.
**Don't** load fonts, icons or images from third-party hosts.
**Don't** mark a statement or callout with a thick colored side border; use the 3px black section rule or type instead.
